notes: Read SKILL.md and references/api_endpoints.md, authentication.md, core_capabilities.md, eventbridge.md, sdk_reference.md in full. The skill documents the Benchling Python SDK 1.25.0 and v2 REST API for registry entities, inventory, notebook entries, workflow tasks, events (EventBridge) and warehouse access.

Following it, the agent installs pinned packages (`uv pip install "benchling-sdk==1.25.0"`, `biopython`), reads BENCHLING_* credentials from the environment, calls the user's live Benchling tenant, and may perform tenant writes (create/register/update/archive entities, container moves, check-in/out, material transfers, workflow-task status changes) and write local files such as sequences.csv. This is medium risk but acceptable: it is the user's own integration task, packages are pinned from PyPI, the workflow says read a small page before writing and read back results (SKILL.md:65-70), and the references warn against printing secrets/headers (authentication.md:103-104) and against sending credentials to URLs found in event data (authentication.md:131, eventbridge.md:73).

Mutating examples (archive, transfers, workflow status) act on real lab records; users should confirm IDs and intent before running them. The SKILL.md:178-193 citation section asks the agent to add a citation of the K-Dense paper to deliverables it materially contributed to (and fetch the arXiv record), telling the user it did so. eventbridge.md:126-148 includes two short JSON EventBridge filter patterns labelled '(from Benchling docs)'; they are a few lines of functional configuration and are treated as de minimis.
